short.title: Qin Palace Under Desert Sands #Shorts
short.hook: Ancient relics from the Qin Dynasty were discovered beneath the Mao Wusu Desert.
script: Ancient relics from the Qin Dynasty were discovered beneath the Mao Wusu Desert.
Archaeologists found dragon-patterned roof tiles and rammed earth foundations.
These materials, rare in lower-level sites, suggest elite royal architecture.
The site had a drainage system and ceramic pipes, indicating full domestic infrastructure.
Few pottery fragments point to a short-lived palace, not a regular settlement.
The site may have been constructed between the 32nd year of Qin Shi Huang's reign and the end of the Qin dynasty, possibly serving imperial travel routes.
Could this palace have been a temporary resting place for Qin Shi Huang's entourage?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A Qin Dynasty royal palace site was found beneath the Mao Wusu Desert in China. The discovery includes dragon-patterned roof tiles, rammed earth foundations, and drainage systems, suggesting elite architectural status. Researchers believe it may have served imperial travel along the Zhidao Road. The site was previously classified as Han, but new evidence points to earlier Qin origins. Source: Vietnam.vn, https://www.vietnam.vn/en/phat-hien-hanh-cung-bi-an-thoi-tan-bi-vui-lap-duoi-sa-mac
Full case file: https://youtu.be/MPYdONlD6A4
Images: Royal Geographical Society / Public domain / Wikimedia Commons; Segalen, Victor (1878-1919). Photographe / Public domain / Wikimedia Commons
